speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Again. From the breath, Nick. Not from the throat.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I had it, and then the height took it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Sing it on the breath, not on the height. She's fourteen, not a whistle.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I can hold it if I come in under the note, sir. If I come in on it, it goes.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Then you come in under it, and you stay under it. A full third below every queen you have pitched since you were eleven.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it there. I prefer her so. I am changing no word.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: You hear him. Under the note. She will sound graver than her mother, and that is what he wants.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: Graver than her mother. I can do graver. I cannot do a whistle and a girl in the same breath.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: If she is graver than her mother, what is a page supposed to sound like?

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: A prince's page should learn to stand still. You fidget, and the yard looks at you instead of at her.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: I stand still when the line is mine. The line is not mine. Waiting has elbows.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Elbows in. The roll is hers. You are the still point at the edge of it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Two-and-thirty days of mornings to the sixth of December. We will spend them on the breath, not on a new speech.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two-and-thirty mornings. No new speech. She is fourteen, and the words stand.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I will not shout it across this afternoon's battles. I am not in the battles. I am in this roll.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: And I am in it only to stand. I can stand.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Arthur is at the back. He is not your concern. Eyes on the lute.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I am not looking at Arthur. I am looking at the note.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep looking at it. If you come in on it, it goes. You have already said so.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Once more, under. Then the afternoon may have the stage, and we are done with this roll until tomorrow.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: Under. I have it.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: I will stand at the side. I will not invent a page's feet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Feet still. That is the lesson, and it costs nothing.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Good. Two-and-thirty, and not a morning wasted on a whistle.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: Not a whistle. A girl, if the lute stays down.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The lute stays down. The words stay. Go and be still until you are called.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: Still. I heard it the first time Nick shouted it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Then both of you have heard it. Off the stage. The hired men want the floor.
